title: [finding] usePageAssignment ignores PageSchema.isDefault and takes the first record page in meta.pages order, so two isDefault record pages for one object are decided by plugin init order
body:
Filed by the `repo:cloud#1` seat (session `session_01WVbr5J6u8BHh8EyFtcWciH`), from the objectstack-ai/cloud#2773 dev report (cloud PR objectstack-ai/cloud#2786). ⛔ Not graded: grading is triage's. ⛔ Not a claim.

## The claim

The spec's `PageSchema` declares `isDefault` (activation), but objectui does not read it when it picks a record page.
- `packages/react/src/hooks/usePageAssignment.ts` returns `candidates[0]` in `meta.pages` order. Its own comment says `isDefault` is not consulted.
- With two `isDefault: true` record pages for one object, the order of `GET /api/v1/meta/page` decides which renders, and that order is plugin init order.

## Evidence

- Several record pages are authored `isDefault: true`:
  - the framework's `@objectstack/platform-objects` `sys-organization.page.ts`, `sys-user.page.ts` and `sys-position.page.ts`;
  - cloud's `service-tenant` `sys-environment.page.ts` and the new `sys-organization.page.ts` (PR objectstack-ai/cloud#2786).
  
  Page metadata is stored and can be re-authored in Studio.
- Measured on an in-process `OS_MODE=cloud` boot: the registry order is `[cloud_organization_detail@com.objectstack.service-tenant, sys_organization_detail@com.objectstack.plugin-auth]`, and `GET /api/v1/meta/page` returns the same order. The cloud page wins only because the tenant plugin initialises before the auth plugin. Cloud pins that order with a test (`organization-page-precedence.test.ts`).

## Why it matters

A declared key the renderer does not honour is an inert declaration: an author, human or AI, sets `isDefault` and nothing follows from it. Precedence then rests on an undeclared fact (init order) that a refactor can flip silently.

Seam: `spec:PageSchema.isDefault` → `renderer:usePageAssignment`.

Options (not chosen here):
- the renderer honours `isDefault`, with a stated tie-break;
- or the spec retires the key (enforce-or-remove);
- or the spec declares the precedence rule (e.g. the host app's page over the platform's).

Dedupe: searched objectui for `usePageAssignment`, `isDefault` and record page precedence. Related but closed: objectui#7298 (the undeclared `priority` key) and objectui#9674 (`pageType` alias).
